finding: Equal nonzero curvature cannot use the zero-curvature third-order witness. A general regular-branch graph derivative also contains tangential acceleration, and its sign can be compared after clearing positive integer powers without squaring.

derivation.definitions: v=C1, a=C2, j=C3, S=v dot v>0, A=cross(v,a), J=S*cross(v,j)-3*A*(v dot a). Use the common positive tangent direction as the x-axis.
derivation.reparameterization: Under a positive source chart derivative lambda, S scales by lambda^2 and J by lambda^6; acceleration terms cancel. Thus J/S^3 is parameter-invariant.
derivation.zero_curvature: A=0 reduces the third derivative to cross(v,j)/S^2, consistent with the corrected squared magnitude denominator S^4.
derivation.signed_comparison: For the same side, compare J1*S2^3-J2*S1^3 directly. Preserve the angular cut and any base-direction conventions when adapting this to traversal.

counterexample_family: C_a(u)=(u+a*u^2,(u+a*u^2)^2) gives A=2, v dot a=2a, cross(v,j)=12a, hence J=0 for every a. This is the same parabola and is covered by V861.
